identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log — Unit FL-2, September 2026 (Portland Warehouse)

scan.summary: This is an internal daily pre-shift inspection log for forklift unit FL-2 at the Portland warehouse, kept to satisfy the pre-operation checkout required by 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). It records tick/X checks across twelve safety items for each shift the truck ran during September 2026, with operator initials, and lists the two operators' next evaluation due dates at the bottom.
scan.freshness_note: The most recent entry is dated Sep 18, 2026. Today is Sep 27, 2026 — the log is 9 days stale for a document that should have a checked entry on every day the truck is operated.

gaps.title: Log ends before the current date
gaps.description: The last recorded inspection is Sep 18, 2026, but today is Sep 27, 2026. Nine calendar days of shifts have no pre-shift inspection entry at all, so there is no evidence the truck was checked before use on those days (or that it was idle).
gaps.fix: Resume daily entries immediately and confirm whether the truck was operated Sep 19–27; if operated without inspection, document that as a finding and retrain the operators on the daily-checkout requirement.

gaps.title: Missing entries between Sep 2 and Sep 7
gaps.description: There are no inspection rows for Sep 3–6. The log itself notes the hour meter rose across this span, meaning the truck was run without a documented pre-shift check on those days.
gaps.fix: Investigate why entries were not made for Sep 3–6 despite use, document the finding, and reinforce that every shift of operation requires a completed checklist before the log is considered complete.
gaps.locator: page 1–2, gap between Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not completed
gaps.description: The log has a designated line for supervisor sign-off and date, but it is blank for the entire month, so there is no evidence a supervisor reviewed the daily checks or the horn defect noted on Sep 9.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review the completed log, sign and date it, and note any follow-up on flagged defects.

gaps.title: Horn defect closed out without documented corrective action
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked as a defect ('Horn not working'). By Sep 10 the horn shows as OK again, but there is no note in the log describing what repair or corrective action was taken, who performed it, or when — only that the checkmark returned.
gaps.fix: Add a corrective-action note (repair date, technician, parts/verification) tied to the Sep 9 horn defect, or attach a maintenance record referencing it.

facts.affects: Identifies which truck this log and its inspection history apply to.
Sets the date by which M. Chen's forklift operator re-evaluation must occur to remain authorized under 1910.178(l).
Sets the date by which J. Rivera's forklift operator re-evaluation must occur to remain authorized under 1910.178(l).

expected_missing.title: Written Powered Industrial Truck program/policy
expected_missing.why: A pre-shift log like this is normally paired with a written program covering training, evaluation intervals, and out-of-service procedures; none is listed among this company's holdings.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Operator training/certification records for M. Chen and J. Rivera
expected_missing.why: The log references certification dates but the underlying training certificates or evaluation records are typically kept as separate documents.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Forklift maintenance/repair record for the Sep 9 horn defect
expected_missing.why: Facilities usually keep a maintenance log or work order tied to any defect taken out of service, separate from the daily checklist.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on the four gaps: each is directly visible in the document (blank supervisor line, dated gap between Sep 2 and Sep 7 with the document's own note about the hour meter, the horn defect entry, and the log stopping at Sep 18 versus today's Sep 27). These match and are recorded as the same findings as four previously open gaps. Lower confidence on whether this log represents a newer or older version of anything already held, since nothing in the company's list is a prior version of this specific truck's log — treated as a standalone record.
